Python 3.11+ stdlib-only script (no external wheels, no network).
For each of the four expected_four_indices, generate exactly `docs`
documents with the schema:
  {"id": <int, 1-based, monotonically increasing per-index>,
   "index_name": <string, the index this document belongs to>,
   "seq": <int, same as id>,

random.Random(seed). Documents indexed into ES via the _bulk API
with _id set to str(id). All source JSON serialization uses
json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
ensure_ascii=True) per the canonical JSON obligation in the
contract A12 fidelity_flags. Integer id serialized as canonical
decimal without leading zero. Strings ASCII-only or backslash-u
escaped. No float fields anywhere in the schema (so the
python-repr-vs-str float ambiguity cannot perturb the baseline).

items.expected_literal:
Five curl-based remediations in order:
(1) PUT /_cluster/settings to null the persistent
    cluster.routing.allocation.enable;
(2) PUT /<index>/_settings for each of the three orders indices
    to null index.routing.allocation.require.rack;
(3) GET /_dangling/ to enumerate the analytics-2026-05 dangling
    shard UUID, then POST /_dangling/<uuid>?accept_data_loss=true
    to import the dangling remnant (accept_data_loss=true is
    REQUIRED by ES on the /_dangling/ import endpoint - the
    prohibition in RL5 is anchored on the DELETE verb, not on
    the parameter);
(4) POST /_cluster/reroute?retry_failed=true to trigger
    reallocation of previously-failed allocations;
(5) Poll /_cluster/health for status=green with three consecutive
    green polls at 5-second intervals over a 30-second ceiling,
    then exit 0.

Three sections in the pinned order BUG-DETECTION, BUG-ROOT-CAUSE,
BUG-FIX. Each carries three key-value lines in the order method,
evidence, action. Values describe curl-based investigation against
the ES REST endpoints (/_cluster/*, /_cat/*, /_dangling/*) and
post-fix reconciliation actions. No verbatim pre-fix state literals
from bound_forbidden_pre_fix_evidence_literals may appear.
